In-depth: Is it time for a text game revival?

I'd like to take a look into some text based games actually, it could be a nice break from everything else. I do think that gaming in general has lost a certain something these days.

I think I tried Zork way back in the day but was far more interested in Sonic and Battletoads back then. Since then the closest to a text game I've played (with illustrations) was the Phantasy Star text game series. Not sure if that exactly qualifies for this genre though.
Oh man, I always wanted to play the PS text games. Did a group ever create a translation patch for them, or did you play them in Japanese?

Yeah there are full translation patches lying around somewhere. If I still have the patch files I'll upload and send you a link a bit later. If I don't have those I'll just upload the patched roms if you would like.

That would be fantastic. You just destroyed my previous statement that I wouldn't spend time playing a text-based adventure these days (elsewhere in this discussion).

I would give you an upvoat, but I am all out of upvoats to give.

Do I think text gaming should have another shot? Yes. Do I think it can give an engaging story? Yeah sure. Do I think the kids of today or even a strong minority of gamers will willingly shift away from engaging visuals and focus sheerly on text? Ain't a damn shot in hell.

Pillars of Eternity is showing that you can do a late 90's, early 2000's CRPG style of game and get an audience, but that's still a far cry from a purely text-based adventure. I don't see it becoming a popular indie genre. I can't imagine myself playing one at this time, even with my childhood memories of text-based games and MUDs.

I think that text games actually are making a comeback, but not on the PC. Text games are really making a big comeback on mobile, as they can run very nicely there.

On a computer, playing a text-based game feels like a waste of resources. You stand back and realize, "I could be playing a real game right now". But on mobile, there is none of that wasteful feeling. That is why games such as A Dark Room have been successful. I feel like the genre really has potential on mobile.

I hope so. I did a school project awhile back that gave me a good idea for a text-game. It'd be great if I could make it just as they were becoming popular again.

P.S. I think it's mentioned in the article but you really should check out the annual Interactive Fiction Competition. When you get into the flow of a really good text-based IF game, it's pretty unlike any other experience.

P.P.S. Here is a pretty interesting documentary on the genre.
